title: Lifting a prescribed finite-free derived model across a nilpotent quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset R$ an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$, assume every element of $1+I$ is a unit, and let $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded-above complex of finite free $R/I$-modules, and let $\alpha:K\otimes_R^L R/I\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(F^\bullet)$ be a specified isomorphism, where $Q$ denotes passage from complexes to the derived category and derived scalar extension is as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the one-object site with only the identity covering. There exist a bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules, an isomorphism $\beta:Q(P^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ in $D(R)$, and an isomorphism of complexes $\theta:P^\bullet\otimes_R R/I\xrightarrow{\sim}F^\bullet$ such that $Q(\theta)=\alpha\circ(\beta\otimes_R^L R/I)$ under the canonical identification $Q(P^\bullet)\otimes_R^L R/I\cong Q(P^\bullet\otimes_R R/I)$. If $F^i=0$ for $i>b$, $P^i$ can be chosen zero for $i>b$.

source.place: Tag 0H76, lemma-check-pseudo-coherent-modulo-nilpotent; Tag 0BCB, lemma-lift-complex-stably-frees; prescribed-isomorphism form furnished by the choice of delta in the proof of lemma-lift-complex

proof.text: By pseudo-coherence choose a bounded-above finite-free complex $L^\bullet$ and $\gamma:Q(L^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Tensor with a free module is a direct sum of copies of the input, so it preserves exact sequences. Thus $L^\bullet$ is K-flat by the bounded-flat-complex lemma, and its termwise reduction $\overline L$ computes derived reduction. Put $\eta=\alpha\circ(\gamma\otimes_R^L R/I):Q(\overline L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(F)$. The projective-complex map-representative lemma, applied over $R/I$ to the bounded-above finite-free complex $F$, gives a chain map $\delta:F\to\overline L$ with $Q(\delta)=\eta^{-1}$. It is a quasi-isomorphism since its cohomology maps are those of an isomorphism in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 0BCA (lemma-lift-complex), cone construction and cokernel proof; Tag 0BC9 (lemma-lift-acyclic-complex)

proof.text: Use the class $\mathcal P$ of all projective $R$-modules. It is closed under finite sums and summands: lift a map from a sum componentwise, and a map from a summand by precomposing with the retraction. For any module $M$, $M/IM=0$ implies $M=IM=I^NM=0$. Consequently a map surjective modulo $I$ is surjective, by applying this argument to its cokernel. Every term of $F$ lifts as $R^{r_i}$ and every term of $\overline L$ lifts as $L^i$. The cone-properties lemma gives the bounded-above acyclic complex $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta)$, with $C^i=\overline L^i\oplus F^{i+1}$ and each term reducing a member of $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 0BCA (lemma-lift-complex), cone construction and cokernel proof; Tag 0BC9 (lemma-lift-acyclic-complex)

proof.text: The three hypotheses of the acyclic lifting lemma are exactly the projectivity, summand closure and reflection of surjectivity verified in step 2. Apply it to $C$ to obtain a bounded-above acyclic complex $A$ of projective $R$-modules and a complex isomorphism $e:\overline A\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. No finiteness of $A$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 0BCA (lemma-lift-complex), cone construction and cokernel proof; Tag 0BC9 (lemma-lift-acyclic-complex)

proof.text: Apply the strict-map lemma to $L$, $A$, $C$ and the cone inclusion $j:\overline L\to C$. It supplies $f:L\to A$ with $e\overline f=j$. Set $B=\operatorname{Coker}(f)$ degreewise. The cone-cokernel lemma identifies $\overline B$ with $F[1]$ and says the reduced right-exact sequence $L^i\to A^i\to B^i$ is split exact. Choose this identification explicitly: in $e$-coordinates the image of $\overline f$ is the first summand of $C^i=\overline L^i\oplus F^{i+1}$, so $[x,y]\mapsto y$ defines a bijection $\rho^i:\overline B^i\to F^{i+1}$. Since the second coordinate of the cone differential is $-d_Fy$, these bijections form a chain isomorphism $\rho:\overline B\xrightarrow{\sim}F[1]$. Its first two terms are projective; its last reduction is the reduction of the finite free lift $R^{r_{i+1}}$ of $F^{i+1}$. Apply projective-class reduced splitting in every degree. Hence $0\to L\xrightarrow f A\to B\to0$ is degreewise split exact and every $B^i$ is projective. Set $P=B[-1]$ and $\theta=\rho[-1]:\overline P\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, using the canonical cancellation of opposite shifts.

source.place: Tag 0BCA (lemma-lift-complex), cone construction and cokernel proof; Tag 0BC9 (lemma-lift-acyclic-complex)

proof.text: For each $i$, lift a finite basis of $F^i\cong P^i/IP^i$ to $P^i$. If $M_i$ is their span, the cokernel $T=P^i/M_i$ satisfies $T/IT=0$, hence $T=I^NT=0$. Thus $P^i$ is finite. It is projective by step 4, and its reduction is free, so the finite-projective-free-mod-ideal lemma makes it free, using precisely the hypothesis that every element of $1+I$ is a unit. If $F^i=0$ for $i>b$, the same nilpotent argument gives $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. For a literal zero module above $b$, put $P^{\prime i}=P^i$ for $i\leq b$ and $P^{\prime i}=0$ otherwise. Let $u^i:P^{\prime i}\to P^i$ be the identity below the bound and the unique isomorphism above it; define $d_{P\prime}^i=(u^{i+1})^{-1}d_P^iu^i$ and $\theta^{\prime i}=\theta^i\overline{u^i}$. Then $d_{P\prime}^{i+1}d_{P\prime}^i=0$ by cancellation of $u^{i+1}$, and $u$ is a chain isomorphism, so the later isomorphism $\beta$ is replaced by $\beta\circ Q(u)$ and the marking equation follows by composing with $Q(\overline u)$.

source.place: Tag 0BC6 (lemma-isomorphic-finite-projective-lifts), and Tag 0H76 proof, nilpotent Nakayama argument

proof.text: Let $D=\operatorname{Cone}(f)$, with $D^i=A^i\oplus L^{i+1}$ and $d(a,l)=(d_Aa+f(l),-d_Ll)$. There are chain maps $t:D\to B$, $t(a,l)=[a]$, and $p:D\to L[1]$, $p(a,l)=l$. The cone triangle $L\to A\to D\xrightarrow{-p}L[1]$ and the derived-cohomology long exact sequence show that $-p$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since $A$ is acyclic. Also $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its kernel identifies with the complex of pairs $(x,l)\in L^i\oplus L^{i+1}$ with differential $(d_Lx+l,-d_Ll)$ and contraction $(x,l)\mapsto(0,x)$. Explicitly, a cycle of $B$ lifts to $z\in D$; $dz$ lies in that kernel and its contraction subtracts a kernel element to make $z$ closed. A closed element of $D$ whose image is a boundary in $B$ differs, after subtracting a lifted boundary, by a kernel cycle, which is a kernel boundary. This proves bijectivity on cohomology without assuming reduction is exact on arbitrary sequences. Define $\beta=\gamma\circ Q((-p)[-1])\circ Q(t[-1])^{-1}:Q(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$.

source.place: Tag 0BCA (lemma-lift-complex), cone construction and cokernel proof; Tag 0BC9 (lemma-lift-acyclic-complex)

proof.text: It remains to check the prescribed marking, including its sign. All of $L,A,B,D$ are bounded-above complexes of projectives, which are flat: by the summand characterization, tensoring with a projective is a retract of tensoring with a free module, and hence preserves exact sequences. Thus bounded-flat K-flatness and derived change of rings compute the reduction of $\beta$ by the displayed chain maps. In coordinates supplied by $e$, $\overline D^i=\overline L^i\oplus F^{i+1}\oplus\overline L^{i+1}$ and its differential is $(x,y,z)\mapsto(d x+\delta y+z,-d y,-d z)$. The map $\rho\overline t$ is $(x,y,z)\mapsto y$ and $\overline p$ is $(x,y,z)\mapsto z$. The degree-minus-one map $h(x,y,z)=x$ to $\overline L[1]$ satisfies $d h+h d=\delta[1]\rho\overline t+\overline p$. Therefore $Q(-\overline p)=Q(\delta[1])Q(\rho\overline t)$. Shift by $-1$ and cancel $Q(\overline t[-1])$ to obtain $\beta\otimes_R^L R/I=(\gamma\otimes_R^L R/I)\circ Q(\delta)\circ Q(\theta)$. Since $\alpha\circ(\gamma\otimes_R^L R/I)\circ Q(\delta)=\eta\eta^{-1}=1$, this is exactly $Q(\theta)=\alpha\circ(\beta\otimes_R^L R/I)$.
